correctness.rationale: For every algebraically closed K and r>=2, the explicit matrix commutators reduce to three wedge equations. The d!=0 nonzero-(a,f) locus is irreducible of dimension 3r+3 by a constant-rank bundle. The d=0 locus is an irreducible Grassmann-incidence image of dimension 3r+3; its quadric fibers are irreducible in all characteristics. The a=f=0 locus is linear of dimension 4r. The three loci cover all solutions, and explicit inclusion/noninclusion checks show precisely two components at r=2 (using a direct one-parameter degeneration of the linear family) and three for r>=3. Independent exhaustive tests verify defining equations and point counts for q=2,r<=4 and q=3,r=2. Finite checks alone do not prove irreducibility.

originality.rationale: The classification identifies all reduced irreducible components, their defining geometric families and dimensions, for every tuple length r>=2 and arbitrary characteristic. Closest primary work concerns a two-element commuting graph (Majeed/Ramkumar), odd-characteristic branching counts (Kaur/Sharma/Singh), pair-scheme complete intersections in characteristic zero (Li), and full-nilpotent-cone commuting varieties (Levy/Ngo/Sivic). Those statements do not imply the claimed component classification. The motivating paper remained partially inaccessible, and alternative historical formulations are a residual risk.

value.rationale: An exact irreducible-component classification for Hom(Z^r,U4(K)), all r>=2 and all characteristics, is a natural structural invariant of a noncommutative unipotent algebraic group. The number of components jumps from two to three at r=3, and the unique maximal-dimensional linear component emerges at r>=4. These facts are not routine deductions from a pair commuting graph, a complete-intersection statement for r=2, or a finite-field branching matrix, and they provide usable strata for subsequent geometric and representation-theoretic study.
